approach: Add a reading-time cap check in reading.rs, and pin the budget values inside each test helper so tests stop reading the live job_usd. (1) New `check_cap_budget(reading, config)` in reading.rs. It applies to a reading that has a capability, no question, and `athena.toml` listed as a Modify deliverable. It scans the reading's summary, assumptions and criteria for proposed values of `reader_usd`, `producer_usd`, `verifier_usd`, `job_usd`, `planner_usd`, `critic_usd` and `max_rounds`. Accepted forms are `key = N`, `key: N`, `key to N`, `key at N` and `key from A to N`, with an optional `$` and backticks; the last mention wins. It overlays those values on a clone of the base `Config` by plain assignment, then calls `Config::check_budget()`, and on `ConfigError::BudgetBelowReserve` refuses with the `required` figure from that error as `$N.NN`. It never calls `budget_required` or sums caps itself, because `no_second_sum_of_stage_caps_in_core` (run/tests.rs:12005, CONFIG_SUMS at 11839) forbids both in core production code. A new `accept_with_budget(...)` runs `refusing_check` and then `check_cap_budget`. `read_once` (reading.rs:732) calls it, so a refusal takes the existing path: `ReadError::Refused`, then `read_for` rereads once with the refusal text (reading.rs:541-577). The refusal rule name is `check_cap_budget`, stored in `ReadingRefusal` and counted by status.rs:227. (2) Tests: config.rs, reading.rs, admission.rs and run_pin_tests.rs get a pinned-budget helper over the live `athena.toml` text. It rewrites the `reader_usd`, `producer_usd`, `verifier_usd` and `job_usd` lines, plus `[job_plan]` `planner_usd`, `critic_usd` and `max_rounds` where a test sums them, to fixed values. The job_usd-dependent assertions then use that fixture, and each file gets a test that rewrites the live job_usd line to 60.00 and shows the fixture is unchanged. Full-suite independence (criterion 3) also needs two shared test seams outside the four named files: `repo_with_config_and_models` in run/tests.rs:309 and `test_config()` in athena-cli/tests/common/mod.rs:37. Both feed tests that assert dollar figures around 50.00 (run/tests.rs:2540-2547, 10546, 10578; athena-cli/tests/drain.rs:5449). Pinning them there is the one-line fix. The producer proves it by running `cargo test --locked` with athena.toml job_usd temporarily set to 60.00, fixing any further test by pinning in its helper, then reverting athena.toml, so athena.toml has no net change. The existing candidate-time admission check (admission.rs:929-958) keeps its behavior; only its test stops depending on the live value. CHANGELOG.md records the change and the intended refusal rate, and docs/decisions.md gets an appended D190.

decisions.choice: Put the new check in reading.rs as `check_cap_budget`, called from `read_once` through `accept_with_budget` right after `refusing_check`. Do not add it as a `step!` in `refusing_check`.
decisions.reason: `refusing_check` and `check_reading_acceptance` (reading/checks.rs:492-551) take no `Config`. A step there needs a config parameter on both. That means edits to checks.rs, reading/replay.rs:55, refusal_corpus.rs (run() at 2770 and the wrapper test at 2801), and about 100 `check_reading_acceptance(..)` call sites in reading.rs tests. checks.rs and refusal_corpus.rs are not deliverables. `build_reading` already holds config-dependent refusals outside the chain (`check_reading_size`, reading.rs:822-831), and the refusal reaches the same correction retry. It is enforced in code, not in prose. Consequence: criterion 1 names `check_reading_acceptance`, but the tested entry point is `accept_with_budget`; this is raised as a User question.

rejected.why: Touches non-deliverable files and about 100 call sites. The corpus guard `every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case` (refusal_corpus.rs:2905) would also demand a new corpus case in a file outside scope.

`plan_findings` has no config and its caller is planning.rs:500, outside the deliverables. The existing candidate-time admission check still catches a plan whose caps overshoot, after production. This is recorded as a risk.

rejected.option: Compare the sum in a new function that re-adds the caps
rejected.why: The scan test no_second_sum_of_stage_caps_in_core fails on it, and criterion 5 forbids re-deriving the sum.

decisions.choice: Take `required` from `ConfigError::BudgetBelowReserve { job_usd, required, short }` (config.rs:605, 948-957) returned by `Config::check_budget`.
decisions.reason: Production core may call neither `budget_required` nor any other CONFIG_SUMS method outside `budget_reserve` (run/tests.rs:11839, 11965). `check_budget` is not in that list, and its error already carries the figure that `budget_required` computes. Tests may call `budget_required` directly to compute the expected value independently.

rejected.why: Valid and allowed, but it gives no short figure and no tolerance rule; `check_budget` is the same function admission uses at admission.rs:937.

decisions.choice: Read proposed values from the reading's own text (summary, assumptions, acceptance criteria). When no value is recovered, or `athena.toml` is not a Modify deliverable, the check does nothing. When the reading proposes `job_usd`, that value is used as the job budget; otherwise the base `job_usd`.
decisions.reason: A Reading has no structured field for proposed config values (records.rs:444-482), so text is the only source. Failing open on unrecoverable values keeps the check from refusing readings it cannot judge, as the reading assumption says. Overlaying only what is stated on the base config means a reading that quotes an existing value changes nothing.

rejected.option: Add a structured `proposed_caps` field to the reading schema
rejected.why: Changes the reader schema, the Reading record and the reader prompt budget (docs/system-facts.md budgets are at 1998 of 2000 for the reader). Far beyond the request.

decisions.choice: Pin each test's budget values inside its own helper, as a fixture over the live text: `pin_budget` in config.rs tests, `fixture_config` in reading.rs tests, a pin in `config()` in run_pin_tests.rs, and a derived value in the admission test. Keep one real-config test per place that asserts `check_budget().is_ok()` on the live file and no value.
decisions.reason: This keeps tests that need the other live sections (models, checks, classes) while removing dependence on job_usd and the caps summed in the assertions. A config-only raise of job_usd then touches no test. The one live-file test is the guard that catches an athena.toml whose caps exceed its own job_usd.

risks.risk: The text parser misses a form in which a reader writes a proposed value (for example prose like `raise the producer cap to twelve dollars`), so a reading over budget is accepted.
risks.mitigation: The check fails open and the existing candidate admission check still refuses after production (admission.rs:929-958), which is today's behavior. The parser handles the six forms in criterion 2 and tests each. Not measured: how often readers use another form.

risks.risk: False refusal: a reading quotes an old or hypothetical value, such as `was producer_usd = 80.00`, and the overlay pushes the sum over job_usd.
risks.mitigation: The last mention of a key wins, and the refusal text prints the exact values it read, so the reader's one correction reread can restate. The check applies only to a Modify deliverable athena.toml, and the expected share is about 1% (an estimate, not measured).

risks.risk: A reading that proposes caps and the base job_usd is raised by a later job in the same plan or drain (jobs landing in order) is judged against the base config of its own commit.
risks.mitigation: Every job reads its configuration from its own base commit (athena.toml header comment, lines 3-5), so judging against the job's base is the same rule admission uses.

risks.risk: Pinning the budget in shared test helpers could hide a real mismatch between the live athena.toml and its own caps.
risks.mitigation: Keep `the_shipped_config_covers_its_own_caps` in reading.rs and the config.rs live-file test asserting `check_budget().is_ok()` on the live text, so the real file is still checked and its value is not asserted.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests in reading.rs plus a wired test in run_pin_tests.rs. In reading.rs, `fixture_config()` is the live athena.toml with its budget pinned (reader 2, planner 3, critic 3, 5 rounds, producer 10, verifier 5, job_usd 50). The test builds `governed_reading(&["athena.toml", "CHANGELOG.md"], &["athena.toml sets producer_usd = 20.00", ...], &[])`, calls `accept_with_budget(reading, request, None, &[], None, &fixture_config())`, and expects `Some(("check_cap_budget", error))`. The expected figure is computed in the test by assigning producer_usd = 20.0 on a clone of the fixture and calling `Config::budget_required()` (57.00); it asserts the message contains `$57.00`, `job_usd`, and a hint to raise job_usd. The wired test in run_pin_tests.rs uses a `reader_proposing_caps` tweak (same shape as `reader_refused_then`, run_pin_tests.rs:1931) that sets the first reading's deliverables to athena.toml and its first criterion to `athena.toml sets producer_usd = 60.00`. The second reading is clean. `athena.ask` runs the real `read_once`, `read_for` and `reading_attempts` (2018).
demonstrations.observes: The unit test sees refusal rule `check_cap_budget` with `$57.00` equal to the independently computed `budget_required`. The wired test sees reading attempt 1 refused with rule `check_cap_budget` and text naming `$67.00` (reader 2 + producer 60 + verifier 5; `config()` has no [job_plan]), then attempt 2 accepted, with the reader run twice.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without `check_cap_budget` wired into `read_once`, the reading is accepted: the unit test gets `None`, and the wired test finds attempt 1 accepted with no refusal and the reader run once.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points: `accept_with_budget` (new, added in step 2) and `Athena::ask` -> `read_for` -> `read_once` (exists, reading.rs:524-583). Fixtures: `fixture_config()` is a reading.rs test helper added in step 5, passed as the `config` argument. The wired test injects the `reader_proposing_caps` Tweak through `athena_with(..)` (exists, run_pin_tests.rs:154), added in step 7, against `config(true)` (exists, line 80). The refusal logic stays in production code; the doubles only supply the reading text and the config.

demonstrations.method: Companion tests in reading.rs. (a) Proposed caps within budget, such as `producer_usd = 12.00` with the fixture needing 49.00 <= 50.00, are accepted: `accept_with_budget` returns `None`. (b) A reading that proposes both `producer_usd = 20.00` and `job_usd = 60.00` is accepted (57 <= 60), and one proposing `job_usd = 40.00` is refused naming $47.00. (c) A reading that lowers a cap is accepted. (d) A reading without `athena.toml` as a deliverable but with cap-like text (a `src/x.rs` deliverable saying `producer_usd = 99`) is accepted. (e) `athena.toml` listed with text naming no cap field is accepted. (f) Forms `key: N`, `key to $N`, `key from A to N` and backticked keys are each recovered. (g) A key as the suffix of another identifier (`my_producer_usd = 99`) is not read. (h) A reading with `question` set or no capability is skipped. Existing reading tests are untouched.
demonstrations.observes: Accept cases give `None`; refuse cases give `check_cap_budget` with the exact required figure; every other check's outcome for these readings is the same as before (`refusing_check` is unchanged).
demonstrations.fails_without: If the check refused every athena.toml reading, or ignored the proposed job_usd, cases (a), (b) and (c) would be refused. If it ignored `deliverables`, case (d) would be refused.
demonstrations.seam: `accept_with_budget` and `fixture_config()`, as in criterion 1 (step 2 adds the function, step 5 the fixture). Readings come from the existing `governed_reading` helper (reading.rs:4647), which exists.
